SMTO-SKL-0099 — Microsoft sent back a reply SMTO couldn't safely use

GUID: 677335fa-197e-51a6-913d-81d1b3a08d92
Slug: microsoft365-provider-response-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Microsoft answered, but the answer was in an unexpected shape or pointed somewhere SMTO doesn't trust. SMTO stopped instead of using it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you asked the Agent to change something, check Outlook or OneDrive to see whether the change is already there. SMTO stopped before it could confirm the result, so the change may or may not have happened.
  2. Ask the Agent once more to do the action, but only if you've confirmed the change isn't already there. Odd replies from Microsoft are sometimes one-off, and checking first avoids doing things twice.
  3. If it happens again, select Copy error details in this panel. This error alone does not establish a repair you can safely make yourself; the details show which Microsoft 365 action got the unexpected reply.

What success looks like

  • The Agent completes the request and shows the result.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO; this may be a problem SMTO needs to fix. Don't paste passwords, codes or secrets into the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Graph response validation failed: a returned URL was outside pinned Graph/transfer hosts, a status/body/collection could not be parsed as the expected result, or a download returned a non-200 status.

What this means

  • Graph URL/transfer validation rejects unsafe returned locations, or HTTP/body/collection validation cannot interpret the response as a supported result. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph URL/transfer validation rejects unsafe returned locations, or HTTP/body/collection validation cannot interpret the response as a supported result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe shape/status information and destination constraints without following untrusted locations.

How to fix it

  • The error carries no Graph details (provider_diagnostics is attached only to successful results), so identify the operation from the Run's tool call: a graph_url/transfer_url rejection means Graph returned a nextLink, Location or uploadUrl outside graph.microsoft.com/v1.0 or the allowed SharePoint/OneDrive hosts, and otherwise a read got an unexpected status or unparseable body. For a write, read the exact resource before any new write. Report a repeatable failure as a bug with the operation name.
  • Inspect the recorded response-validation condition and exact resource; use only supported provider locations and reconcile any prior write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported same-scope response validates before further access.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
